messages:
customer-jane: Hey team — starting ~10:32 UTC we're seeing p99 latency jump for eu-west-1 requests to ~1.2s (usually ~60-120ms). No obvious errors, just slow. Traces show an unexpected hop to us-east-1. Can someone look?

support-luke: Sorry you're hitting that, Jane. Can you paste an example request id or raw trace? Also which model + API path?

customer-jane: endpoint: POST /v1/generate, model: redwood-mosaic-8k, x-request-id: req_01F8XYZ, sample curl: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ****" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-mosaic-8k","prompt":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Trace link (obfuscated): https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/01F8XYZ

sre-ana: Got the trace. Short excerpt below (simplified):
```
edge-eu-west-1 (ingress) -> router-eu-west-1 -> policy-check -> egress-us-east-1 -> model-pool-us-east-1 (serve)
```
This matches what you saw — request is egressing to us-east for serving.

support-luke: Any idea why routing sent it cross-region? Models should be available eu-west.

eng-mohit: Quick theory: the routing policy has a fallback that picks "nearest compatible" model when a pinned variant isn't available in-region. If eu-west model variant was temporarily drained, the policy might choose the us-east variant. I'm checking autoscaler/allocations.

infra-bot: [allocations] model redwood-mosaic-8k@eu-west-1 = 0/4 replicas healthy between 10:30-10:36 UTC; draining -> scaled up us-east replica pool.

eng-mohit: Confirmed — eu-west pool momentarily reported unhealthy during a maintenance window, and fallback routing defaulted to "global-compat" which prefers lower-cost regions. That policy was recently bumped in canary.

support-luke: Workaround for now: you can pin region from client side with header `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1` or set model param `region:\"eu-west-1\"`. If the region is forced, we'll return 503 if not available instead of failing over. Want me to enable that stricter behavior for your org?

customer-jane: Yes please — we'd rather get errors than 1s tail latency. Also would like repro steps so we can validate after changes.

sre-ana: Steps to repro and validate:
1) repro: run 5 sequential requests without region header and observe trace showing egress-us-east-1.
2) mitig: add header `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1` to same requests. Trace should show final serve node in eu-west.
3) verify: p95/p99 should drop back to ~100ms.
Example curl to pin region:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-mosaic-8k","prompt":"latency test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

eng-mohit: We're rolling a config change to routing canary to tighten fallback behavior (set fallback_preference: local_region_first). Command: `redwoodctl rollout config routing --canary=1 --set=fallback_preference=region_local` (will propagate in ~4m).

infra-bot: Rollout started: routing-config v2026.03.17-canary-7 -> canary=1 -> target=eu-west-1, propagation expected 4m.

support-luke: Jane — I flipped org-level stricter routing for you (opt-in) so pinned region returns 503 if not available. Please test with the pinned header.

customer-jane: Testing now... pinned header run 1: p99 88ms. run 2: 95ms. Nice, thanks.

sre-ana: We'll keep monitoring traces and autoscaler logs for the eu-west pool. If you still see cross-region egress, ping this thread and include a sample x-request-id.

eng-mohit: Root cause summary: eu-west pool briefly became degraded during maintenance; new canary routing default favored global fallback that picked us-east replicas. Fix: tighten fallback preference + alert on replica drain to avoid cross-region failover for low-latency tiers.

customer-jane: Appreciate the quick help. Please keep me posted if the canary exposes any regressions. :thumbsup:
